title: Morgan Reyes
about: I currently lead People Ops at a ~200-person startup, where I own everything from hiring to comp bands to the offsite nobody wants to plan.

Before this, I spent four years as a recruiter — two agency-side, two in-house — and a year doing HR generalist work at a company that taught me how fast "culture" turns into paperwork if you're not careful.

I got into this field by accident, covering for a manager on leave, and stayed because I like the part of work everyone else finds tedious: the systems underneath how people actually get hired, paid, and treated fairly.
I think most HR problems are really trust problems wearing a policy costume.
interests: Hiring systems — structured interviews, scorecards, and how to make a process fair without making it soulless.
Compensation design, especially the tension between internal equity and staying competitive for scarce roles.
Manager development. Most companies promote their best individual contributor and call it leadership training.
People analytics, used carefully — attrition and engagement data can tell real stories, but they lie easily if you let them.
The parts of company culture that get built by accident versus the parts anyone actually designed on purpose.
